clue.text: Very hot American crooner embracing surgeon

indicators.note: the crooner's name wraps its arms around the surgeon's, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
Joseph Lister, the pioneering British surgeon of antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A heatwave report featuring an American singer hugging a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby was the classic American crooner; Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery. 'embracing' wraps the singer round the surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistering weather is scorching, hot enough to raise blisters on the skin.

clue.text: Bishop going to pub brings a sneer

indicators.note: the bishop goes to the pub, so his letter is attached at the end of it

parts.note: a bar is a pub
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman heading for the pub attracts some contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' places B after BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting, wounding remark, much the same as a sneer.

clue.text: Earnestly ask to be given stuff like fairy stories?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous fairy-like sprite
lore is a body of traditional tales and knowledge

explanation.surface: Begging to be told fanciful tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'stuff like fairy stories' reads as IMP LORE, traditional tales about imps; 'to be given' and 'stuff like' simply join.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg or plead with someone urgently.

clue.text: Show girl's date

definitions.meaning: a stage musical by Sandy Wilson, a 1950s West End hit
the young man a girl is going out with

explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous musical, and also literally the male partner a girl dates.

clue.text: Roguish friend with nasty scar on head

indicators.note: in this down clue the jumbled scar sits on top of the friend, at its head
a nasty scar is a damaged one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A mischievous pal with an ugly scar on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns SCAR into RASC, and 'on head' sets it above ALLY in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascally person behaves like a rascal: mischievous and dishonest.

clue.text: Port's knocked over — Virginia gets in a state

indicators.note: Virginia gets into the overturned port, so its letters go inside
in a down clue knocking something over turns it upside down, so the port is read backwards

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Some fortified wine has been spilt and a Virginian gets agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink and 'in a state' as being upset; Aden is a port in Yemen, and 'knocked over' suits a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, in the American West.

clue.text: Attempt to make sailor follow someone good

indicators.note: the sailor follows the good person, so his letters come after

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a supremely good person
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Trying to get a seaman to tag along behind a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good person; 'follow' puts the sailor last.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab at something is a try or go at it.

clue.text: Vehicle taking soldiers south of area

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers come below, so after, the area

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A truck carrying troops below some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' sets OR beneath TRACT in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a farm vehicle used to pull machinery.

clue.text: Long hair on little boy — initial objection supported

indicators.note: in a down clue the long hair sits on top of the little boy

parts.note: 'but' is a word of objection, as in 'no buts', and here it opens the answer
a tress is a long lock of hair
Ed, short for Edward, is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small boy with flowing locks meets early resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'on' means stacked above; 'initial' tells you the objection comes first, before the hair and the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttressed means propped up or reinforced, as a wall is by a buttress.

clue.text: With respect to newspapers I have become tyrannical

parts.note: re means regarding or with respect to
the press is newspapers collectively
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claims the newspapers have turned them into a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A repressive regime is tyrannical, crushing freedom and dissent.

clue.text: Floating structure right behind

parts.note: aft means behind, toward the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A dock sitting just to the right rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat platform that floats on water.

clue.text: Country cart overturned — there are lots of police here

definitions.text: there are lots of police here

parts.note: Scotland is a country of the UK

indicators.note: in a down clue an overturned cart is upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart, traditionally for brewers

explanation.surface: A Scottish farm cart has tipped over and the police are swarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns DRAY into YARD. Scotland Yard is the London headquarters of the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, where many officers are based.

clue.text: Crazy thing to put on the railways

definitions.text: thing to put on the railways
definitions.meaning: a short form of locomotive, an engine running on rails

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for insane and also an abbreviation of a railway engine.

clue.text: Bad actor, I fancy, should be one to resign

indicators.note: to fancy can mean to imagine, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre critic thinks a poor performer ought to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges BADACTORI. 'should be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An abdicator is someone who gives up a throne or position, stepping down from office.

clue.text: Recruits for the war study texts

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study carefully
scripts are written texts

explanation.surface: New soldiers read up on documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts are people compulsorily enlisted into the armed forces, often for wartime.

clue.text: Stuff too much in maiden maybe — female then unwell

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A young woman is crammed full, then the woman feels sick.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket over is a set of six balls bowled; a maiden is one with no runs. 'in' and 'then' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To overfill is to cram or load something beyond capacity.

clue.text: Supplies rushed on board ship

indicators.note: something on board a ship sits inside it, so these letters are enclosed

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship
tore means rushed or sped

explanation.surface: Provisions hurried aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the standard crossword ship; 'on board' means inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stores are provisions or stocks kept for use.

clue.text: One toils to produce an anagram crazier than anything else!

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the words are rearranged to give the answer

explanation.surface: Someone labours to make a word puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is unusually blunt: it names the device itself. Rearranging ONETOILS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of loony, meaning the maddest or most foolish of all.

clue.text: Girl given greeting after work in London region

indicators.note: the greeting and work sit inside the London region

parts.note: SE, South East, is a postal region of London

indicators.note: the greeting comes after the work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A girl is welcomed once she has finished her job in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' orders the greeting behind the work, and 'in' sets both between the letters of the London region, the South East postal area.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophie is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Awkward fit getting into cloak — unexpected difficulty

indicators.note: the jumbled fit goes into the cloak, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a pall is a cloak or mantle, also a cloth over a coffin

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily mixed up

explanation.surface: A badly fitting cape struggles to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' scrambles the word fit; 'getting into' puts that inside the cloak, a pall being a mantle or coffin cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or trap one stumbles into.

clue.text: Firm fellow, revolutionary behind native American group

indicators.note: the revolutionary is placed behind, so after, the firm and fellow

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a man is a fellow
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A company man trailing behind a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts CHE after COMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

clue.text: Woollen jacket, very loud, available in the capital

parts.note: a cardi is a cardigan, a knitted woollen jacket
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A garish knitted top on sale in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available in' links. 'the capital' is fair since Cardiff is the capital of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Usin' a cycle to go over island, one now uninhabited

indicators.note: in a down clue the cycling piece is placed over, on top of, the island

parts.note: bikin' is riding a bike, with the dropped g mirrored by usin'

explanation.surface: A colloquial cyclist rides across to a deserted isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Usin'' signals the dropped g of BIKIN'. Bikini Atoll in the Pacific was evacuated for nuclear tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a Pacific atoll whose people were moved away for nuclear testing, leaving it empty.

clue.text: Memory of school punishment with new head installed

indicators.note: the first letter of the punishment word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: detention is being kept in after school as a punishment

explanation.surface: Recollections of being kept in after class under a new headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new head installed' swaps the opening D of DETENTION for R. 'new head' tempts as a new headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the ability to keep things in mind, so a power of recall.

clue.text: Dreadful wrath faced by daughter

indicators.note: the wrath is faced by the daughter, who stands in front of it

parts.note: ire means anger or wrath

explanation.surface: A girl confronts her parent's terrible anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced by' puts D in front of IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means terrible or appalling.

clue.text: Learning never ends for the boss

indicators.note: the word for learning never reaches its end, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: study means learning

explanation.surface: A boss insists that education should continue for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ends' cuts the final Y from STUDY. 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface.

clue.text: Design kitchen container to hold litre

indicators.note: the container holds the litre, so it goes inside

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container

explanation.surface: Drawing up a kitchen pot sized for a litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' puts L inside PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or drawing showing a design.

clue.text: Rigid person of the word, a little sir being silly

indicators.note: the words are acting silly, so they are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pedantic schoolboy is acting the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being silly' rearranges ALITTLESIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A literalist sticks rigidly to the exact wording, taking things at face value.

clue.text: Only person to be heard

indicators.note: the word is listened to, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

explanation.surface: The sole person anyone could hear.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL and SOLE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or one and only.

clue.text: Dido's feted when in action in musical festival

indicators.note: the words are set in motion, moved around into a new order

parts.note: Dido's supplies its letters including the S

explanation.surface: A famous queen is celebrated when she performs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' rearranges DIDOSFETED. 'when' links. An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eisteddfod is a Welsh competitive festival of music, poetry and song.
